arguments.new:
def split_row(line: str):
    """Split one CSV line into fields. Fields may be double-quoted; inside a
    quoted field a comma is literal and a doubled quote is a literal quote."""
    fields = []
    field_chars = []
    in_quotes = False
    field_was_quoted = False
    i = 0
    while i < len(line):
        c = line[i]
        if c == '"':
            if in_quotes:
                # If doubled quote inside quoted field, append one literal quote
                if i + 1 < len(line) and line[i + 1] == '"':
                    field_chars.append('"')
                    i += 1
                else:
                    # closing quote
                    in_quotes = False
            else:
                # starting quote for this field (only valid at field start)
                # treat as quoted field and do not include the quote itself
                in_quotes = True
                # mark that this field was quoted so we won't strip whitespace
                field_was_quoted = True
        elif c == ',' and not in_quotes:
            text = ''.join(field_chars)
            if not field_was_quoted:
                text = text.strip()
            fields.append(text)
            field_chars = []
            field_was_quoted = False
        else:
            field_chars.append(c)
        i += 1

    # append last field
    text = ''.join(field_chars)
    if not field_was_quoted:
        text = text.strip()
    fields.append(text)
    return fields

arguments.summary: Implemented CSV-aware split_row: parse character-by-character tracking quoted fields, handle doubled quotes as literal quotes, preserve commas inside quotes, and strip whitespace for unquoted fields. Tests pass.
